newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia economy on verge of breakthrough - premier.
newsitem.headline: Russia economy on verge of breakthrough - premier.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday that structural reform had put the Russian economy on the verge of a breakthrough.
But he told the cabinet industry still faced huge financial problems, and called on the regions to pursue reforms themselves while urging the Federal Bankruptcy Agency to be tougher.
"We're on the point of a breakthrough. We can raise up the Russian economy and make it competitive and respected throughout the world. But it could work out differently," he said.
Industrial production has been growing and in June was two percent higher than a year earlier, he noted.
But government forecasts submitted to the meeting said industrial output over the whole of this year would not rise and could fall by up to two percent.

Chernomyrdin said a new cycle of serious structural reform had begun but he said debts of Russian companies had almost doubled in the first half of this year to 27 percent of gross domestic product from 15 percent.
Profits in real terms were 2-1/2 times lower than a year ago.
Government budget revenues were improving, but over the first half of the year were only 64 percent of budgeted levels, forcing the government to cut spending to 68 percent of budget, he said.
Chernomyrdin called on regional governments to continue reforms.
"The centre asks for only one thing -- don't stand still. Build your own reform programmes," he said.
He also called on the Federal Bankruptcy Agency to deal more harshly with copmanies who owed taxes to the government.
